("Brothers" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *Commander of the 39th Household of [[Inwit]] *[[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Imperial Fists]] *[[Master of the Fleet]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Imperial Fists]] |Notes = }} '''{{PAGENAME}}'''{{Fn|3}} was a [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] Commander of the 39th Household of [[Inwit]] in the [[Imperial Fists]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], who held the title of [[Fleet Master]] during the closing years of the [[Great Crusade]].{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|4}} ===Biography=== Before he became an Imperial Fist, Yonnad was amongst the hundreds of [[aspirant]]s that trained under the watchful eye of the [[Primarch]] [[Rogal Dorn]] after he was reunited with his Legion in 835.[[M30]]. During his training, Yonnad formed a friendship with fellow Aspirants '''Kye''' and '''Archamus''', but their friendship would soon be severed by the actions of Kye. During a combat exercise with [[Combat Servitor]]s, Archamus was killed after he followed a strategy created by Kye that went against what their superiors overseeing the exercise had told them to follow. Yonnad held Kye responsible for Archamus' death and their friendship ended, though they remained cordial with each other as they continued their training. Eventually, both were part of the first group of twenty Aspirants that successfully completed their training under Dorn's guidance, and Yonnad was there to witness Kye change his name to [[Archamus]], to honour their fallen friend, during the ceremony welcoming them into the Imperial Fists Legion.{{Fn|1a}} Yonnad would go on to have an distinguished career during the Great Crusade and took many Captains under his wing in order to teach them the art of space combat.{{Fn|1b}} During the Crusade's [[War of the Consus Drift]], his [[Primarch]] gave Yonnad command of the Imperial Fists' forces as they invaded the [[Driftborn]]'s asteroid cities. Even as he did so, Yonnad regretted that the Driftborn's foolish refusal to accept the [[Imperium]]'s [[Compliance]] led so many of them to needlessly die. He was relieved when the Driftborn later surrendered, after Dorn had threatened them with extinction if they continued to resist. Though it saddened him to admit it, Yonnad knew he would have destroyed the Driftborn without hesitation, if his Primarch had willed it.{{Fn|3}} During the [[Araneus Wars]], Yonnad was charged with the mission of prosecuting the war against the [[Araneus Continuity]]. After preparing his forces, Yonnad left [[Tallarn]] with a force of 20,000 Space Marines alongside millions of troops of the [[Imperial Army]] and the [[Mechanicum]] . The entire force struck as one, overwhelming the peripheral territories of the Continuity in a single day. The Imperial Fists were able to rapidly secure the Continuity's Warp Gates, preventing them from reinforcing themselves. Within two months the Continuity was reduced to a single world, [[Araneus Prime]]. With no other choice, the Technonobility surrendered.{{Fn|4}} When the [[Horus Heresy|Heresy]] began, Yonnad was given command of his Legion's [[Retribution Fleet]], which was sent by [[Rogal Dorn]] to confront [[Horus]] in the [[Isstvan System]]. However, after the Retribution Fleet entered the [[Warp]], it was hit by [[Warp Storm|severe storms]] that wreaked havoc upon it, causing numerous casualties and destroying many of the [[Imperial Fists]]' ships. When the Retribution Fleet finally exited the Warp in the [[Phall System]], it was discovered that Yonnad was among the many Imperial Fists that were killed by the storms. After the remnants of the Retribution Fleet were reformed, command of the remaining ships fell to Captain [[Alexis Polux]], who was Yonnad's current protégé and amongst the greatest of his pupils.{{Fn|2}} ===Sources=== *1: [[Praetorian of Dorn (Novel)]] **{{Endn|1a}}: Part 1 — ''Gifts of the Father'' **{{Endn|1b}}: Part 3 — ''Brothers of War'' *{{Endn|2}}: [[The Crimson Fist (Novella)]], ''One hundred and forty-one days before the Battle of Phall'' *{{Endn|3}}: [[The Will of the Legion (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|4}}: [[The Horus Heresy Book Three - Extermination]], pgs. 76-77 {{DEFAULTSORT:Yonnad, Hashin}} [[Category:Characters (Great Crusade)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Imperial Fists)]] [[fr:Hashin Yonnad]]

Hasik Noyan-Khan.wikitext:
{{WhiteScarsPortal}}
'''Hasik Noyan-Khan''' was a member of the [[White Scars]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]]. Alongside Chief [[Stormseer]] [[Targutai Yesugei]], [[Giyahun]], and [[Qin Xa]], Hasik was one of [[Jaghatai Khan]]'s original comrades, fighting alongside him during the conquest of [[Chogoris]].{{Fn|1a}}

By the end of the Crusade, Hasik was a '''Noyan-Khan''' ([[Lord Commander]]) of his Legion, commanding the [[Horde of the Stone]] with 20 Brotherhoods. Hasik, assisted by [[Hibou Khan]] and [[Torghun Khan]], was the main architect of a plot during the Heresy to take control of the White Scars fleet while it was at [[Prospero]] and ally with [[Horus]].{{Fn|1b}} However the plot [[Second Battle of Prospero|was foiled]] by [[Shiban Khan]]. Upon returning to the ''[[Swordstorm]],'' the Khagan immediately accosted and questioned Hasik. The Noyan-Khan first sought to defend himself with words, but drew his blade when Jaghatai raised his own. The Primarch impaled Hasik with his [[power sword]], and the other conspirators such as [[Goghal Khan]], Hibou Khan, and Torghun Khan all surrendered themselves.{{Fn|1c}} Hasik was not killed by the blow,{{Fn|1d}} but was dead by the time of the events surrounding the Legion's return to Terra several years later;{{Fn|2}} whether this was due to the effects of the Khan mortally wounding him, the judgments that followed the trials after the insurrection was put down, or some other cause is not currently known.

Four years after his death, his successor was [[Ganzorig Noyan-Khan]].{{Fn|2}}

("Father" via [[Gene-Seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *[[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Sons of Horus]] [[4th Company (Sons of Horus)|4th Company]] *Member of the [[Mournival]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by =[[Garviel Loken]] |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Sons of Horus]] ***[[4th Company (Sons of Horus)|4th Company]] ***[[Mournival]] |Notes = }} '''Hastur Sejanus''' was the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[4th Company (Sons of Horus)|4th Company]] of the [[Luna Wolves]] [[Space Marine Legion]] and a member of the [[Mournival]]. A senior commander and particularly close friend to his [[primarch]], [[Horus]], he was murdered during compliance negotiations upon [[Sixty-Three-Nineteen]].{{Fn|2a}} His appearance was later used by [[Erebus]] in an attempt to trick and coerce Horus into following the path of [[Chaos]]. ===History=== Captain Sejanus served as praetor of the Fourth Company and stood at Horus's side during the Luna Wolves' joint undertaking with the [[Blood Angels]] to subjugate the [[Nephilim]] species on [[Melchior]]. He fought with 8,000 legionaries, and he was wounded by a shreikpulse weapon during the campaign.{{Fn|5}} Considered a senior lieutenant to Horus since at least the time the Luna Wolves waged war against the [[Keylekid]] species, Sejanus notably became a close comrade to [[Phosis T'Kar]] of the [[Thousand Sons]] during T'Kar's secondment to his legion.{{Fn|1a}} Their bond of brotherhood was renewed during the [[Ullanor Triumph]], which both captains attended as part of their respective primarch's inner circles{{Fn|1b}}. In the wake of the great Triumph, Sejanus commissioned the making of four rings, for himself and the three other members of the [[Mournival]], from a silversmith [[remembrancer]] attached to the [[battle barge]] ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]''. Unfortunately, Sejanus's ring was destroyed, and the other three presumably lost, when he rushed into the remembrancer's shop to aid the smith, whose throat had been fatally crushed by Captain [[Targost]].{{Fn|4}} A little over a year after the Ullanor Triumph, in the 203rd year of the [[Great Crusade]], Captain Sejanus was given the honour of making the first face-to-face contact with the ruler of the planet later known as Sixty-Three-Nineteen. Unfortunately, a mis-step in diplomacy resulted in the murder of Sejanus and his retinue. The legion considered his death a tragedy, and the manner of it (ambushed and hacked down during a diplomatic treaty) caused particular outrage. [[Warmaster]] Horus, who was said to have loved Sejanus like a son and to have campaigned with him across one hundred worlds, ordered that Sejanus's murderers, the [[Invisibles]], be decimated. Sejanus's position in the Mournival was later taken by Captain [[Garviel Loken]].{{Fn|2a}}{{Fn|2b}} [[Word Bearers]] [[Chaplain]] Erebus assumed Hastur Sejanus's form during his coercion of Horus to Chaos during the Warmaster's treatment in the [[Serpent Lodge]] on [[Davin]], in an attempt to beguile the Warmaster by presenting his guide in the spirit realm as the shade of a close friend.{{Fn|3}} ===Appearance and Abilities=== Noted as the commander's favourite and a perfect captain, Sejanus was a popular figure in the [[Luna Wolves]]. Both an accomplished diplomat and warrior, with a martial record second only to that of First Captain [[Abaddon]]'s, Sejanus was described as being a particularly handsome and noble man of balanced humours, with Captain Loken going so far as to say that there was no finer figure in [[Power_Armour#Mark_4_.22Imperial_Maximus_Suit.22|Mk. IV plate]].{{Fn|2a}} He had widely set eyes that glittered silver, and a firm straight nose that mirrored that of the Luna Wolves Primarch Horus{{Fn|3}}. He had very dark skin and a short comb of grey hair running down the center of his scalp.{{Fn|6}} ===Trivia=== {{Trivia}} *[[Wikipedia:Hastur|Hastur]] is the name of a senior, malignant entity in [[Wikipedia:H.P. Lovecraft|H.P. '''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the 3rd [[Fellowship]] of the [[Thousand Sons]] [[Space Marine Legion]] during the [[Great Crusade]]. Maat was also the Magister Templi of the [[Pavoni]]. He escaped the [[Burning of Prospero]] as part of the contingent teleported from the planet by [[Magnus]] to the [[Eye of Terror]].

=== Background ===
Like his fellow captains, he had secondment with another legion. He is known to have spent time serving with the [[Emperor's Children]] Legion. Maat was noted to be exceptionally proud of an [[Oath of Moment]] attached to his breastplate. It had been personally carved by [[Fulgrim]] himself.{{Fn|1b}} He was described as being vain and proud{{Fn|1c}} yet exceptionally handsome and stereotypically heroic looking with golden hair.{{Fn|1d}}

He was the Magister Templi of the [[Pavoni#Cult_of_the_Pavoni|Cult of Pavoni]]{{Fn|1e}} and a powerful psyker whose abilities focused primarily on the ability to heal{{Fn|1f}} although he was also known to have the ability to channel potent offensive lightning spells.{{Fn|1g}} Maat was present with the Legion while serving as part of the [[28th Expeditionary Fleet]]. And took part in the campaigns on [[Aghoru]] and [[Ark Reach Secundus]]. He participated in the failed defence of [[Prospero]] and was last noted to be present amongst the surviving members of the Thousand Sons who escaped to the [[Planet of Sorcerers]].{{Fn|1h}}

Maat was one of the Captains who [[Ahzek Ahriman]] knew would be easy to sway to his Cabal to stop the flesh change.{{Fn|1j}}

Maat accompanied Ahriman on his quest to track down the [[Shards of Magnus]]. However, he began to suffer from the flesh change. Striking a bargain with the [[Daemon]] [[Aforgomon]] and [[Lucius the Eternal|Lucius]] accompanying Ahriman's cabal, Hathor Maat learned to hold off the flesh change by sacrificing captive humans. Aforgomon further manipulated Hathor Maat into altering a single line of the [[Book of Magnus]]. However when Ahriman's cabal finally came to the shards of Magnus at [[Nikaea]], the change began finally overcame Maat. Paying the price owed to Aforgomon, Ahriman sacrificed Hathor Maat to allow the daemon to take over his body and manifest as the [[Kairos Fateweaver|Fatewoven]] (which as it seems was the same '''Kairos Fateweaver''' in disguise, as well as Aforgomon).{{fn|2}}

===Trivia ===
{{Trivia}}
''Hathor'' is a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hathor major goddess in ancient Egyptian religion]. She was, amongst other roles, the mother or consort of the sky god ''Horus'' and the sun god ''Ra'' and symbolic mother of their earthly representatives, the pharaohs. She also crossed boundaries between worlds, helping deceased souls in the transition to the afterlife. ''Maat'' likewise is an [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maat Egyptian goddess] and personifies the concepts of truth, balance, order, harmony, law, morality, and justice. She also regulated the stars, seasons, and the actions of mortals and the deities who had brought order from chaos at the moment of creation.

Heathobar.wikitext:
{{DeathwatchPortal}}
'''Heathobar''' was an [[Iron Lords]] [[Deathwatch Librarian]], in the [[Eye of Octos]] [[Watch Fortress]]' [[Watch Company|Company Secundus]].{{Fn|1b}}
==History==
The [[Watch Company]] was commanded by [[Watch Captain|Captain]] [[Daox Glykas]], who joined his forces with those of [[Inquisitor]] [[Athocles Van Roth]] in [[M42]]. The Inquisitor then used this combined strike force to defend himself, as he sought to master using [[Baddkrasha's Crown]] on the [[Ork]] and [[Tyranid]] infested [[Maiden World]] [[Veloria]]. However using the [[Xenos]] device, drew numerous Ork warships to the Crown's location. Their fleet retreated to avoid being destroyed, but Van Roth came up with a plan to allow his forces to escape. For it to succeed though, it would require them to work with [[Eldar]], they discovered had been left stranded on Veloria. When Glykas later told his Watch Company of this, many were against it working with the Xenos. He was ultimately swayed to follow Van Roth's plan by [[Heathobar]] however. Doing so, the [[Psyker]] explained, would give them the best chance to prevent the Orks from reclaiming the Crown, which the Watch Company had first taken from [[Big Mek|King Mek]] [[Baddkrasha]]. With the decision made, Glykas would take a portion of the Watch Company, to aid Van Roth and the Eldar. Meanwhile, Heathobar was given command of another portion of the Company and possession of the Crown itself. He was to use it, to lure the newly arrived Orks into the numerous Tyranid swarms on Veloria. Heathobar succeeded in doing so, but only he was able to escape the massive melee between the Xenos, that followed. However when he then returned to Van Roth's camp he saw that it was being overrun. While he was using the Crown to lure the newly arrived Orks, it had done the same for the Orks that were already on Veloria. This had led the Xenos directly to the camp and, with their fleet also being overwhelmed, Van Roth's forces were not able to escape from the Maiden World.{{Fn|1a}}

'''Hebet Zybes''' was a citizen of [[Calth]], who worked as a farmhand, when the [[Word Bearers]] [[Battle for Calth|attacked]] the world, during the [[Horus Heresy]]. As the invasion raged, Zybes soon joined a small group of Imperials who escaped with the [[Perpetual]] [[Ollanius Persson]], into a [[Warp Rift]] he created.{{Fn|1a}}
===History===
This began a journey through time and space, as [[Ollanius Persson]] tried to reach [[Terra]] before the traitorous [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]] could kill the [[Emperor]]. In order to do so, Persson had to use a [[Athame]] ritual blade to create numerous temporary [[Warp Rift]]s, to travel through. However soon afterwards, the group began to be pursued by a [[Daemon]] who sought to stop them before they reached Terra. No matter how many Warp Rifts they escaped into, the Daemon was able to track the group down and was always close behind them. This led Zybes to be in a constant state of fear, which was not helped when his fellow traveler Katt, discovered she had [[Psychic]] abilities. She would use her powers to determine the length of time it would take before the Daemon reached them, which allowed the group to stay one step ahead of it{{Fn|1a}}. However her abilities led Zybes to fear and distrust her as a [[Psyker|witch]], which in turn eventually led him to begin hating her.{{Fn|1b}} 

Zybes survived the journey to Terra as well as the horrific [[Emperor's Children]] dream-garden known as Paradise. He was able to resist the temptations of the realm as he had nothing left besides Oll and his group.{{Fn|1c}} Zybes accompanied the group into the [[Imperial Dungeon]], eventually reaching the [[Golden Throne]] alongside the other "[[Argonauts]]", but discovering that the Emperor had gone to fight Horus aboard the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]''.{{Fn|2}}

As the group continued on their quest, Zybes discovered a spool of his thread leading a path that [[John Grammaticus]] came to believe was sent by them from the future.{{Fn|3a}} However, they were soon confronted by [[Erebus]] on the walls of the [[Imperial Palace]]. During the subsequent fight most of the group were slain. Zybes was killed when [[Erebus]] used [[Enuncia]] to blow [[Graft]] apart, causing a piece of metal to impale him.{{Fn|3b}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''',{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2}} also known as '''Ushapt-Osiron Hedara Ptomalac''', was a [[Contemptor Dreadnought]] of the [[Thousand Sons]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] and Guardian of the House of the Jackal during the [[Battle of Prospero]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
[[File:Hedara Ptomalac.jpg|thumb|right|275px|[[Ushapt-Osiron]] {{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|1}}]]
Before becoming a [[Space Marine Dreadnought|Dreadnought]], Hadara Ptomalac was part of the first generation of recruits from [[Prospero]] to be inducted into the [[Thousand Sons]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], during the [[Great Crusade]]. Ptomalac is listed as the commander of a [[Heavy Support Squad|heavy support squad]] during the [[Relief of Keene's Landing]], where he also received an Imperial citation. Years later, Ptomalac fell in the battle known as the [[Last Stand on Rakotis]], and was interred into one of the first [[Contemptor Dreadnought]] frames his Legion received.{{Fn|1}}

Ptomalac was later one of a cadre of nine [[Dreadnought]]s that served as the ritual protectors of the [[House of the Jackal]], a large mortuary and memorial complex on the western edge of [[Tizca]]'s central district on [[Prospero]] (and also "slept' there). During the [[Battle of Prospero]], when the invading [[Space Wolves]] had already shelled the outer walls of the House of the Jackal into rubble, Hedara Ptomalac and his surviving fellow Dreadnoughts emerged from the ruins and counter-attacked the Space Wolves' heavy armour at short range. Ptomalac was destroyed after personally accounting for two [[Typhon Heavy Siege Tank|Typhon Siege Tanks]].{{Fn|1}}

Heironymo Sondar.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Heironymo Sondar''' was the High Master of [[Vervunhive]] on the planet [[Verghast]]. 

== History ==
Around 679.M41, Heironymo had personally commanded [[Vervun Primary|Vervunhive's army]] during its [[Trade War (Verghast)|Trade War]] against [[Ferrozoica]] Hive Manufactory, which ended when Vervun's troops overran Zoica's defenses.{{Fn|1a}}

Heironymo was an effective and popular leader who created many of the laws that ruled Vervunhive. Around 719.M41, at the age of 120, Heironymo was murdered by his twenty-year-old nephew [[Salvador Sondar|Salvador]], who was jealous of Heironymo's popularity and sought to take control of Vervunhive for himself. Salvador would rule Vervunhive for fifty years afterwards, still bearing the guilt of murdering his uncle, until he himself was killed during the [[Siege of Vervunhive]] in 769.M41. Despite the length of Salvador's reign, Heironymo remained a venerated figure by the people of Vervunhive, much to the chagrin of his successor.{{Fn|1a}}

==Relics==
In addition to his abilities as a leader, Hieronymo was a mechanical genius who created many unique pieces of technology.  One of these was a miniature device that could shut down all of Vervunhive if plugged into a data port.  Hieronymo entrusted this device to [[House Chass]], the most public-minded of the city's noble houses, as a safeguard in case any later High Master of the city became a tyrant (as Salvador did).  [[Ibram Gaunt]] reflected that, in its own way, the device was as deadly as an atomic warhead or a [[Space Marine Chapter]].{{Fn|1b}} After Lord Chass was murdered by Salvador, his daughter, [[Merity Chass|Merity]], entrusted it to Gaunt, who used it to crucial effect in his strike on [[Heritor Asphodel]]'s command vehicle.{{Fn|1c}}

The [[Sword of Heironymo Sondar]] was a revered artifact carried by whoever commanded the defense of Vervunhive. During the Siege, it was carried by Marshal [[Edric Croe]], who passed it on to Gaunt shortly before his own death in the Siege.{{Fn|1d}} Gaunt has carried it with him ever since.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a renowned [[Freeblade Knight]] who pilots the [[Knight Preceptor]] ''[[Canis Rex]]''.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|2}}
'''Canix Rex''' is remarkable that its [[Thunderstrike Gauntlet]] is a unique marvel of technology. Named '''Freedom’s Hand''' it can crush even the most resilient targets delivering them horrible damage.{{Fn|3}}

===History===
Cerberan was a [[Knight]] of [[House Cerberan]] until sometime after the [[Great Rift]]'s creation when his [[Knight World|Homeworld]], [[Randoryn Alpha]], was invaded by the [[Iron Warriors]] forces of the [[Warsmith]] [[Ghanshor]]{{Fn|1a}}. Despite their best efforts, his Household was overwhelmed, until only Hekhtur and a few other Knights remained. The Knights then decided to make their last stand in front of their fortress, the '''Stygian Keep''', but the Warsmith would not be denied Randoryn Alpha and their Knight suits were disabled by invasive electrogheists. With their defeat, Ghanshor now held Randoryn Alpha in his grasp and the captured Nobles began to be tortuously reconditioned. The process began to break the spirits of the Nobles and allowed them to easily embrace the worship of [[Chaos]] and corrupted their Knights into heretical engines of destruction. Soon only Hekhtur remained uncorrupted and he held onto his loyalty to the [[Emperor]], no matter what was inflicted upon him.{{Fn|1b}}

His deliverance later arrived though, when his [[Knight Preceptor]] '''Canis Rex''' activated on its own and freed the Noble. Now the last loyal Knight of House Cerberan, Hekhtur took the oath of the [[Freeblade Knight|Freeblade]] and led the Randorynian resistance, fighting back against the heretics wherever he could. He managed to free many enslaved serfs and then ferried them off-world to safety, earning his Freeblade epithet, '''The Chainbreaker'''. Eventually though, even the grimly determined Hekhtur was forced to accept that the fight for Randoryn Alpha was lost. Rather than throw his life away, Hekhtur took Canis Rex and the small complement of loyal [[Sacristan]]s he had managed to save, and stole an [[Imperial]] [[frigate]] to escape his doomed Homeworld. He now searches for a war that he can win for the Imperium and has voyaged the stars ever since; freeing Imperial citizens enslaved by foul oppressors and punishing the scions of Chaos with vehemence and fury{{Fn|1b}}. His successful efforts have been noticed by the [[Imperium]] and has made Hekhtur Cerberan, a well regarded Imperial hero and a source of inspiration.{{Fn|2}}

Hektur challenged the [[Dreadblade Knight]] [[Hatred of Krastellan]] and the two traded blows on [[Dyseph IX]].{{Fn|4}} He later led a [[Freeblade Lance]] into the [[Ivordex Reach]] and attacked several enemy-held worlds there.{{Fn|5}}

Hektor (Captain).wikitext:
{{UltramarinesPortal}}
'''Hektor''' was an [[Ultramarines]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]], who commanded the [[Battleship]] ''[[Fist of Macragge]]'' and he was charged with searching out lost [[Human]] worlds, during the last years of the [[Great Crusade]].{{Fn|1a}}

==History==
One of these worlds was [[Arkenath]], where Hektor and the five hundred [[Space Marines]] he commanded, waged a three year war that destroyed the [[Vektates]] [[Xenos]] species and freed the Human population they had mind controlled. Afterwards, the grateful Humans of Arkenath eagerly joined the [[Imperium]] and Hektor received new orders from his [[Primarch]] [[Roboute Guilliman]]. He was to immediately journey to the [[Vangelis]] [[Space Station|space port]] to collect Captain [[Lysimachus Cestus]] and his forces there, before joining his Legion at the muster on [[Calth]], as it prepared to attack the [[Ork]] hordes invading the '''Veridan System'''.{{Fn|1a}}

Before the ''Fist of Macragge'' could enter the [[Warp]] however, it was attacked and nearly destroyed{{Fn|1a}} by the [[Word Bearers]] Battleship, the ''[[Furious Abyss]]''. Its commander [[Zadkiel (Word Bearers)|Zadkiel]] had joined his Primarch [[Lorgar]], and the Word Bearers Legion, in turning upon the Imperium and had targeted the ''Fist of Macragge'' in order to field test the newly built ''Furious Abyss''' weapon systems{{Fn|1b}}. With his Battleship now dead, due to the damage it had received, Hektor gave the order to send a warning{{Fn|1a}} to the Vangelis space port{{Fn|1b}} before the ''Furious Abyss'' fired again and completely destroyed the ''Fist of Macragge''.{{Fn|1c}}

Helad Gibran.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Navigator]] of [[House Gibran]] and the [[Paternoval Envoy]] of the [[Navis Nobilite]] in mid-[[M32]] during the [[War of the Beast]].

As the representative of the head of the [[Navigator]] Houses, Gibran held much sway among the [[High Lords of Terra]].{{Fn|1a}} He owed [[Inquisitorial Representative]] [[Wienand]] a favor, which the [[Inquisitor]] believed would lead to him siding with her in any power struggle against [[Lord High Admiral]] [[Lansung]].{{Fn|1b}}

During the war, Gibran worked closely with his allies [[Master of the Adeptus Astra Telepathica]] [[Abdulias Anwar]] and [[Master of the Astronomican]] [[Volquan Sark]] to create an emergency network of immaterial translation routes and astrotelepathic conduits.{{Fn|2}} Later, Gibran was one of the first High Lords to support [[Koorland]], the [[Inquisition]], [[Drakan Vangorich]], and [[Vernor Zeck]] when they removed [[Lord Commander]] [[Udin Macht Udo]] from power.{{Fn|3}}

After the war, Gibran was among the High Lords targeted by [[Grand Master of Assassins]] [[Drakan Vangorich]] in [[The Beheading]]. He and his wife [[Erdacian]] were killed when his fifth cousin, [[Dovrian Ofar]], killed him out of ambition at the behest of Vangorich. The murder of Gibran was approved by the [[Paternova]], who felt that his envoy had been a failure during the war. He was subsequently replaced as Paternoval Envoy by Ofar.{{Fn|4}}

{{ambig|subject=High Marshal|disambiguation=Helbrecht}} {{QuoteBox |quote = '''''"Where the [[Neophyte]] sees only the difficulties and the Initiate only the advantages in any great enterprise, the hero sees both."'''''{{Fn|5}} |}} {{Character |Portal ={{BlackTemplarsPortal}} |Name =Helbrecht |Image =HelbrechtArt.jpg |Caption =Helbrecht |Title = |Homeworld = |Birth =c. (as [[High Marshal (Black Templars)|High Marshal]]) |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Black Templars]] |Notes = }} '''Helbrecht''' is the current [[High Marshal (Black Templars)|High Marshal]] of the [[Black Templars]] [[Chapter]].{{Fn|1}} ==Biography== ===Childhood=== Helbrecht was born in the [[underhives]] of the world of [[Piety]]. Unbeknownst to him, a group of [[Custodes]] of the [[Aquilan Shield]] led by [[Grateion Artabane]] guided by [[Doomscryers]] prophecies watched over and protected him until the [[Black Templars]] recruited him into their [[Chapter]].{{Fn|9}} ===Ascent=== [[Image:Helbrecht6.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Helbrecht]] Helbrecht is best known among his friends and enemies for his violence, stubbornness, and desire to slay the enemies of the [[Emperor]]. The notice he received for his many violent campaigns such as the [[Vinculus Crusade]] aided his rise through the ranks from a mere [[Neophyte (Black Templars)|Neophyte]]. He secured a position in the [[Sword Brethren]] after he slew a [[Vampires|Vampire]] which had risen to power on [[Cephian IV]]. When the crusade's leader, [[Marshal (Black Templars)|Marshal]] [[Daidin]], was killed, Helbrecht was elected in his place.{{Fn|1}} On the death of [[High Marshal (Black Templars)|High Marshal]] [[Kordhel]] at the hands of a [[Chaos Champion]], the [[Marshal (Black Templars)|Marshals]] unanimously chose Helbrecht in 989.[[M41]] to succeed him after the subjugation of the [[Xenarch]]s of the [[Sigilare Nebula]]. He was ritually presented with the [[Sword of the High Marshals]] and immediately led a crusade against the [[Cythor Fiends]] in the [[Ghoul Stars]]. After eight years securing outlying systems, Helbrecht moved on to the homeworlds of the Fiends, only to find them empty. The crusade was cut short when a request for aid came from [[Armageddon]]: [[Ghazghkull Thraka]] had returned and the Black Templars channelled their energies into stopping one of the greatest [[Waaagh!]]s{{Fn|1}}. ===Third Armageddon War=== Helbrecht returned to the ''[[Eternal Crusader]]'' and contacted Marshals [[Ricard]] of the [[Dimaris Crusade]] and [[Amalrich]] of the [[Tiberior Crusade]], ordering them to Armageddon. Upon arrival, Helbrecht assumed control of the space fleet, his skills in space combat honed by directing the vast fleet of the Black Templars, while the two crusades deployed to the surface. Helbrecht worked closely with [[Admiral]] [[Parol]] to storm and destroy Ork [[Rok]]s and ships in an effort to stem the tide of reinforcements. When Ghazghkull's suspected command ship was seen retreating from Armageddon, Helbrecht swore an oath to pursue and destroy him. As a sign of respect, he allowed [[Commissar]] [[Yarrick]] to accompany him on the crusade.{{Fn|1}} Helbrecht, accompanying Commissar Yarrick, pursued the infamous [[Ork]] [[Warboss|Warlord]] Ghazghkull Mag Uruk Thraka. However while they were able to corner his flagship [[Kill Wrecka]] at the [[Battle of the Haunted Gulf]], Ghazghkull was able to escape into the [[Warp]] and begin his [[Great Waaagh!]].{{Fn|4}} [[Image:Helbrecht Art.jpg|right|thumb|High Marshal Helbrecht]] ===Slaughter at Schrodinger VII=== Helbrecht commanded [[Battle of Schrodinger VII|the crusade]] that came to the aid of the [[Ice World]] of [[Schrodinger VII]]. The [[Necron]] [[Phaeron]], [[Imotekh]] the Stormlord of the [[Sautekh Dynasty]], had already shifted his armies into defensive configurations. Helbrecht's assault bogged down in a series of impeccably placed ambushes on the [[drop pod]] and [[Thunderhawk]] drop zones and Helbrecht and Imotekh met face to face on an ice bridge. They traded blows until Helbrecht collapsed but, instead of finishing him, Imotekh severed his right hand so he would always be reminded of the humiliation. The Black Templars retreated with Helbrecht, leaving Schrodinger VII in the Stormlord's hands.{{Fn|2a}} Following a five year Crusade of penitence to atone for his defeat, Helbrecht made a pilgrimage to the [[Phalanx]] to pray at the hand of [[Rogal Dorn]]. There, the Chapter Master came to realise that the loss of his hand was symbolic of his Primarch's sacrifice and a sign from the [[Emperor]]. Helbrecht's faith returned to him.{{Fn|3}} ===Conqueror's Fall=== Helbrecht, aboard his [[Battle Barge]] ''[[Sigismund (Battle Barge)|Sigismund]]'', later sought revenge for his humiliation by attacking Imotekh's [[Cairn Class Tomb Ship|Tomb Ship]] ''[[Inevitable Conqueror]]'' while en route to [[Davatas]]. [[Boarding Torpedo]] attacks by the Black Templars succeeded in capturing the ship and Helbrecht and the Stormlord came to blows once more, but this time the Marshal was able to use his rekindled faith to prevail. Realising the battle was lost, Imotekh teleported to a nearby [[escort]] vessel to safety, but not before congratulating Helbrecht on 'one victory apiece'.{{Fn|2b}} In a rage that his enemy had escaped, Helbrecht destroyed the ''Inevitable Conqueror'' from the inside out.{{Fn|3}} ===Dark Imperium=== [[Image:HelberchtArt10th.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Helbrecht battles [[Ork]]s{{Fn|13}}]] ====Hunt for the Beast==== In the aftermath of the [[Great Rift|Great Rift's]] creation, the [[Black Templars]] lost contact with several of their [[Crusades]]. Helbrecht, though, still believes the lost Crusades are still alive and are continuing to fight the [[Imperium|Imperium's]] enemies. While he was still hunting for [[Warboss|Warlord]] [[Ghazghkull]], he was visited by [[Lord Commander of the Imperium|Lord Commander]] [[Guilliman]] about several matters concerning his [[Chapter]]. At first, Helbrecht worried the Black Templars would be censured for not following the [[Codex Astartes]] that Guilliman had written, but the Lord Commander made no mention of this. Instead he sought to convince the [[High Marshal (Black Templars)|High Marshal]] to accept the ability to create [[Primaris Space Marines]] and accept the [[Indomitus Crusade|Indomitus Crusade's]] [[Greyshields]] into the Black Templars' ranks. Guilliman did so in person, because the openly fanatical Chapter were deemed amongst the most temperamentally unpredictable in how they would react to the Primaris' creation. The Lord Commander knew that if Helbrecht accepted them, then his approval would spread throughout the Black Templars' forces. The High Marshal readily did so, as he attributed a spark of the [[Emperor|divine]] to the technology to create Primaris.{{Fn|7a}} With that settled, the two then began to clash over Helbrecht's utterly focused pursuit of [[Warboss|Warlord]] [[Ghazghkull]]. The [[Lord Commander]] reminded the High Marshal of the oaths he swore to protect the [[Emperor|Emperor's]] realm, rather than just carrying out his own vendettas. Helbrecht was shamed by Guilliman's words and sought to immediately rectify his failings. The High Marshal then promoted a number of his most seasoned [[Sword Brethren]] to the rank of [[Marshal (Black Templars)|Marshal]] and bade them to muster new [[Crusades]]. The Black Templars' [[Primaris Space Marine|Primaris]] [[Greyshields]] were also mingled into the Marshals' forces to ensure they were accepted. Helbrecht then oath-swore these new Crusades{{Fn|7a}}, including Marshal [[Holgher|Holgher's]] [[Purgus Crusade]]{{Fn|7b}}, to aid all those worlds of the [[Ecclesiarchy]] that lay perilously along the [[Great Rift|Great Rift's]] border. With his duty done, the High Marshal renewed his vow to purse Ghazghkull to the ends of the Emperor's realm and continued his quest to hunt down the Warlord.{{Fn|7a}} As part of [[Indomitus Crusade Fleet Primus]], Helbrecht led a Taskforce which saved the world of [[Sigma-Ulstari]] from [[Tyranid]] and [[Ork]] forces in the [[Octarius War]]. During the battle, Helbrecht slew the [[Warboss]] [[Tuskagrob Wurldkilla]].{{Fn|8}} ====Vision Quest==== Following his encounter with Guilliman, Helbrecht crossed the [[Rubicon Primaris]] and became a [[Primaris Space Marine]].{{Fn|6}}{{Fn|12a}} Shortly thereafter, he received a vision of [[Rogal Dorn]] fighting [[Iron Warriors]] during [[The Scouring]]. The vision climaxed with a warrior with a [[Black Blade]] and a shattered shard of Dorn's armour. Helbrecht came to believe this was divine guidance, and upon consultation with [[Grimaldus]] learned that another brother, [[Bloheim]], had received the vision. They were able to deduce that the vision pointed to the world of [[Hevaran]], which had been the site of a battle between Dorn and the Iron Warriors. Helbrecht saw the vision quest as a form of atonement for his obsessive hunt of Ghazghkull, but Grimaldus framed it as a quest to instead retrieve a relic of Dorn.{{Fn|12b}} Helbrecht, newly christened [[Emperor's Champion]] Bloheim, and Grimaldus undertook their subsequent quest with only a small honour guard. Arriving at Hevaran aboard the [[Nova Frigate]] ''[[Faith Adamant]]'', finding it in a state of ruin since the opening of the [[Great Rift]]. They then travelled to "Golgoth", finding a valley littered with [[Chaos]] effigies and an Iron Warriors presence as the ''Faith Adamant'' was destroyed in orbit.{{Fn|12c}} Stranded, the group then made their way towards Hevaran's [[Astropath]]ic facility, coming under attack by [[Traitor Guard]] under the Iron Warrior [[Lykas]]. During the subsequent fight, Helbrecht was wounded by the Iron Warrior and would have died had it not been for the sacrifice of the [[Sword Brethren|Sword Brother]] [[Nivelo]]. While unconscious, Helbercht received more visions from prior [[High Marshal (Black Templars)|High Marshals]] as well as the spirit of Nivelo, whom he apologized to. Upon awakening aboard the [[Overlord Gunship]] ''[[Flame of Terra (Gunship)|Flame of Terra]]'', the group overheard a broadcast from the ruling Iron Warriors [[Warsmith]] [[Torven Vakra]], proclaiming the planet "liberated" from the Imperium. The group then met with a group of Imperial pilgrims led by [[Laren]], and the Black Templars agreed to lead them in the coming struggle against the Heretics.{{Fn|12d}} Assaulting the Iron Warriors fortress with the pilgrims, the Imperials were able to breach the traitor walls thanks to their fanatical religious zeal. In the central keep, Helbrecht battled Torven Vakra personally as Bloheim reclaimed the lost shard of Dorn's armour and sent out a distress signal at the [[Astropathic Choir]].{{Fn|12e}} Drawing on his immense faith, Helbrecht was able to kill Vakra as the fortress began to collapse around them.{{Fn|12f}} Helbrecht was then pulled from the rubble as the Black Templars left Hevaran for the ''[[Eternal Crusader]]'' with the lost shard of Dorn's armour reclaimed. Afterwards, Helbrecht confided in Grimaldus that the quest taught him that he was a mere instrument of the Emperor and would go wherever he was needed instead of focusing solely on his vendetta against Ghazghkull.{{Fn|12g}} ====Return to Armageddon==== During the [[Season of Blood]], Helbrecht led the [[Helbrecht Crusade]] to [[Armageddon]] to prevent its fall at the hands of a massive [[Chaos]] horde under the [[Daemon Primarch]] [[Angron]]. During the campaign he frequently clashed with [[Space Wolves]] [[Great Wolf]] [[Logan Grimnar]] due to past grievances and the Space Wolf's fear that the Templars would purge Armageddon's civilian population as had happened during the [[Months of Shame]]. Helbrecht oversaw only limited purges based around Hive Infernus, and the two ultimately learned to work together during the final assault on the [[Red Angel's Gate]].{{Fn|11}} ==Wargear== As the High Marshal of the Black Templars, Helbrecht wields the legendary ''[[Sword of the High Marshals]]''. In addition, he is equipped with the [[combi-melta]] ''[[Ferocity]]''.{{Fn|6}} ==Images== helbrecht lg.jpg|Helbrecht miniature (4th Edition) Halbrecht9th.jpg|Helbrecht miniature (9th Edition){{Fn|6}} JoytoyTemplarsHelbrecht.jpg|Helbrecht Joytoy figure{{Fn|10}} ==See also== *[[List of Chapter Masters]] ==Sources== {{Cite}} *{{Endn|1}}: [[Codex: Black Templars (4th Edition)]], pg. 44 *2: [[Codex: Necrons (5th Edition)]]: **{{Endn|2a}}: pg. 26 **{{Endn|2b}}: pg. 27 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Codex: Space Marines (6th Edition)]] (E-Book Edition), pg. 179 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Waaagh! Ghazghkull - A Codex: Orks Supplement (7th Edition)]]{{cite this}} *{{Endn|5}}: [[White Dwarf 313 (UK)]], pg. 79 *{{Endn|6}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/2021/09/20/helbrecht-returns-the-high-marshal-who-leads-his-crusades-from-the-front/ Warhammer Community: Helbrecht Returns, the High Marshal Who Leads His Crusades From the Front (posted 20/9/2021)] ''(last accessed 29th July 2024)'' *7: [[Codex Supplement: Black Templars (9th Edition)]]: **{{Endn|7a}}: pg. 20-21 - ''Era Indomitus'' **{{Endn|7b}}: pg. 22 - ''Purgus Crusade'' *{{Endn|8}}: [[War Zone Octarius - Book 2: Critical Mass]], pgs. 14-17 *{{Endn|9}}: [[Codex: Adeptus Custodes (9th Edition)]], pg. 29 - ''Aquilan Shield: Deeds of Legends'' *{{Endn|10}}: [https://www.joytoy.com/products/black-templars-high-marshal-helbrecht Joytoy Helbrecht] (last accessed 21/7/2024) *{{Endn|11}}: [[Crusade: Armageddon]], pg. 35 *12: [[Helbrecht: Knight of the Throne (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|12a}}: Chapter 1 **{{Endn|12b}}: Chapters 2-3 **{{Endn|12c}}: Chapters 9-10 **{{Endn|12d}}: Chapters 14-15 **{{Endn|12e}}: Chapters 21-22 **{{Endn|12f}}: Chapter 23 **{{Endn|12g}}: Epilogue *{{Endn|13}}: [[Codex Supplement: Black Templars (10th Edition)]], pg. 27 ===Uncited=== {{Uncited}} *[[Codex: Armageddon (3rd Edition)]] , {{Cite This}} *[[Index Astartes II]], "Black Templars" [[Category:Characters (Armageddon Wars)]] [[Category:Characters (Black Templars)]] [[de:Helbrecht]] [[fr:Helbrecht]]

Helena (Imperial Saint).wikitext:
{{AdeptaSororitasPortal}}
'''Helena the Virtuous''' is an [[Imperial Saint]]{{Fn|3}}, who was once the [[Prioress]] of the [[Adepta Sororitas]]'s [[Convent Sanctorum]].{{Fn|4}}


==Biography==
She was raised in the [[Schola Progenium]] on [[Ophelia VII]], where Helena was remarkably gifted in her youth. After 30 years of service in the [[Order of the Key]], she was raised to [[Canoness]]{{Fn|2}} and was responsible for an increase in the power of the [[Ecclesiarchy]]. This was responsible for Helena being the hand-picked successor to become the [[Prioress]] of the [[Convent Sanctorum]], after the death of the previous Prioress. She would come to wield the [[Rod of Grace]]{{Fn|1}} and a [[Sword of Saint Helena|sacred sword]]{{Fn|3}}, although Helena was not trained as a warrior. Despite this, she was known to personally intervene in battles, which allowed Helena to fully display her keen mind and tactical abilities.{{Fn|2}}

Helena eventually died of unknown causes and was later declared an [[Imperial Saint]]. Her remains and sacred relics were buried in a shrine, bearing her name, on the [[Hive World]] [[Acheron IV]]. When the [[Ork]] [[Warboss|Warlord]] [[Uggrot]]'s [[Waaagh!]] later invaded Acheron IV, [[Canoness]] [[Verena Armenii]], of the [[Order of the Argent Shroud]], led a battlehost of her [[Adepta Sororitas|Sisters]] to Helena's shrine, to recover any of Saint's remains. Upon their arrival in the shrine's ruins, the Sisters were soon attacked by an overwhelming Ork force and it was only the discovery of Helena's [[Sword of Saint Helena|sacred sword]] that turned the tide of the battle. As the remnants of the Sisters' force fought the Orks, [[Seraphim Superior]] [[Camille]] used the sacred blade to kill [[Warboss]] [[Grog Chewtops]]. His death caused the Orks to retreat and saved what remained of the battlehost{{Fn|3}}. Along with her sword, Helena's [[Rod of Grace]] was also recovered and has since become a relic of the Adepta Sororitas.{{Fn|4}}  

A [[Reliquary of Saint Helena|reliquary]] containing Saint Helena's relics was once held on [[Tathyan's Reach]]. However after the [[Great Rift]]'s creation, the world was besieged by the hordes of the [[Sorrowsinger]]. During the subsequent [[War of Sorrows]], however, the forces of [[Indomitus Crusade Fleet Quintus]] came to Tathyan's Reach aid. As the two sides clashed, the Fleet's [[884th Cadian Armoured]] [[Regiment]] later saved the reliquary. Thanks to the 884th Cadian's efforts, the [[Reliquary of Saint Helena]] was safely evacuated, though, its present location is unknown.{{Fn|5}}

Hellick Mauer.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
[[Image:MauerArt.jpg|thumb|right|200px|{{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|1}}]]
'''Hellick Mauer''' was a dogged, curious, and exceptional [[Command Prefectus]] [[Boetharch]] investigator, who took part in the [[Siege of Terra]].{{Fn|1}}

As [[Horus]]' [[Siege of Terra|invasion]] raged, she was charged with keeping law and order within the [[Imperial Palace]]'s riotous outer precincts and wards. The dauntless former [[Imperial Army]] soldier was committed to her duty, even though the nature of Mauer's work was often clandestine and unexplained.{{Fn|1}}

During the Siege, Mauer teamed up with the [[Selenar]] Priestess [[Andromeda-17]] in order to investigate the source of madness and despair infesting the minds of the Imperial defenders.{{Fn|2a}} Their investigations led them to [[Blackstone Prison]], where they met with [[Euphrati Keeler]], [[Kyril Sindermann]], [[Amon Tauromachian]], and the imprisoned [[Basilio Fo]].{{Fn|2b}} Mauer convinced Keeler to come to her aid, and escorted her out of the Prison in a convoy. However, the convoy was ambushed by enemy forces. Keeler escaped but Mauer was confronted by a traitor [[Space Marine]].{{Fn|2c}}

Mauer eventually meets up again with Sindermann and Keeler, taking part in the Remembrancers journey into the [[Hall of Leng]] and Kyril's reunion with [[Garviel Loken]].{{Fn|3}} After Loken leaves for the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]'', Mauer and  Sindermann continue to research lore regarding [[Chaos]]. She reads from a book on [[Samus]], inadvertently saving Loken as he battled the Daemon aboard the ''Vengeful Spirit''.{{Fn|4a}} Later, the duo are confronted by [[Azhek Ahriman]] as he searches for knowledge within the Hall of Leng.{{Fn|4b}} After overhearing Ahriman and Sindermann's conversations on the nature of [[Chaos]] and [[Daemon]]s, the [[Sorcerer]] promptly left when Horus was defeated.{{Fn|5a}}

Mauer survived the Siege and left the Hall of Leng with Sindermann in the aftermath of the battle.{{Fn|5b}}

Hemheda Khan.wikitext:
{{WhiteScarsPortal}}
'''Hemheda Khan''' was a [[Space Marine Captain|Khan]] of the [[White Scars]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], who took part in the [[Siege of Terra]].{{Fn|1a}}

==History==
He was among the [[Imperial]]s who were able to retreat within the [[Sanctum Imperialis]], as the [[Imperial Palace]] was overrun by [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]]' [[Traitor]] forces. Once inside, Hemheda was given command{{Fn|1b}} of a [[Denial Company]] by the [[War Court]],{{Fn|1c}} which were patchwork [[Space Marine Company|Companies]] of [[Legionaries]] who had also made it into the Sanctum Imperialis. They were grouped under commanders, whose task was to guard sections of the '''Delphic Wall''', which served as a final defense against the Traitors trying to invade the Sanctum. Hemheda commanded [[Denial 774]], but it did not take an active part in the defense, as it was among the twenty Companies led by the [[Imperial Fist]] [[Praetor (Rank)|Praetor]]-[[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Honfler]]. Following orders laid down by his [[Primarch]], [[Dorn]], Honfler instead held his Companies in reserve until the section of the Wall they defended was breached or scaled atop of by the Traitors.{{Fn|1b}}  

However once it became clear the '''Delphic Wall''' would fall to [[Horus]]' forces, the [[Denial Companies]] were withdrawn by the [[War Court]] into the [[Sanctum Imperialis]], to prepare for its invasion. They were then separated into groups of Companies, who would be commanded by [[Honfler]] or his deputies as they protected certain sections of the Sanctum. Hemheda and the [[Denial 774]] were placed under the companies command of deputy [[Tamos Roch]] and were sent to defend the Sanctum's '''Marnix Confluence'''.{{Fn|1c}} By that point, though, [[Terra]] had become so infused by the [[Warp]],{{Fn|1d}} that the Traitor forces were able to materialize within the Sanctum Imperialis. The Denial Companies and other Imperials within the Sanctum were thus caught off guard, when they suddenly became attacked by the Traitors, even though its doors were still sealed.{{Fn|1e}}

Hermiatus.wikitext:
{{GSCPortal}}
[[File:HermaphageMagos.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Hermiatus, as the Hermaphage Magos{{Fn|4}}]]
'''Hermiatus''' was a [[Heretek|renegade]] [[Tech Priest]] [[Biologis]] whose experimentation with [[Genestealer]]s{{Fn|1a}} led to the downfall of [[Hive Secundus]] on [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]] in 879.[[M41]].{{Fn|2a}} 

==History==
===Tech Priest===
Hermiatus, a brilliant [[Magos Biologis]] of the [[Adeptus Mechanicus]], was  commissioned by the [[Ordo Xenos]]{{Fn|2a}} of the [[Inquisition]] to develop an antigen to counter the [[genestealer]] plague.{{Fn|1a}} 

He selected Necromunda for his research due to its unique genetic records and history of surviving xenos infections. Using data from the Mercator Pallidus and the Chrono Guild, Hermiatus aimed to isolate the genestealer strain and create a solution to inoculate humanity against the plague.{{Fn|2a}}

He set up a secret laboratory in Necromunda’s hive depths, experimenting on infected subjects and captive genestealers. His work was concealed even from [[Lord Helmawr]], with the [[Chrono Guild]] sworn to secrecy under the Inquisition's authority. Despite significant resources, Hermiatus initially failed to achieve his goal, and his frustration led to a critical mistake{{Fn|2a}} as he was accidentally infected by a genestealer sample.{{Fn|1a}} 

The infection began to corrupt his mind and body, and though he attempted to administer his untested antigen, it failed. Realizing the transformation was inevitable, Hermiatus destroyed his laboratory, notes, and experiments before fleeing Necromunda.{{Fn|1a}} Hermiatus was responsible for mutating and releasing the progenitor of the [[Cult of the Second Son]] known as the [[Malstrain Patriarch]].{{Fn|3a}} 

The Inquisition, alarmed by his escape and the threat he now posed as a [[heretic]], launched an extensive search led by High Inquisitor [[Anneth Vestrix]]{{Fn|2b}}. Hermiatus carried not only critical knowledge of the antigen but also secrets of the Adeptus Mechanicus. After weeks of pursuit, they traced him to the [[Beta Magellan]] sector, where he was eventually brought to justice by the [[Inquisition]] and their allies{{Fn|1a}} at [[Gorinum Station]]{{Fn|1b}}, while the now infested Hive Secundus was toppled and a ring of defenses made around its ruins.{{Fn|2b}}

===Hermiatus, the Second Son===
[[file:HermiatusArt.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Hermiatus Reborn{{Fn|5}}]]
Hermiatus, despite being purged by the Inquisition, has left a lingering legacy through his corrupted DNA, which endures within the genestealers of Necromunda. Over time, a mutated psychic entity known as "'''Hermiatus the Second Son'''", "'''Hermiatus Reborn'''"{{Fn|3b}}, or the '''Hermaphage Magos'''{{Fn|4}} has emerged from the racial memory of the [[Malstrain Patriarch]]. This being, a warped facsimile of the original Magos, continues his heretical work as a twisted version of a [[genestealer magus]].{{Fn|3b}} 

Operating with significant autonomy, Hermiatus conducts vile biological experiments to advance the malstrain's development and oversees the spread of its corruption across Necromunda. He commands infected followers and leads corrupted gangs, sometimes venturing beyond the [[Dust Wall]] to extend the influence of the patriarch. Some speculate his resurrection serves to cure or perfect the malstrain, though his ultimate purpose remains steeped in xenos heresy.{{Fn|3b}}

The creature holds a revered status within the xenos cults of Necromunda and possesses formidable psychic abilities. When the Hermaphage Magos discovers a proto-cult deep within a hive, the hybrid creatures instinctively recognize their genetic progenitor and submit to its will. In essence, the creature serves as a conduit for the psychic influence of the [[Malstrain Patriarch|alien lord of Hive Secundus]], allowing this dark entity to see beyond the confines of its radioactive prison.{{Fn|4}} 

As a result, it has become a coveted target for countless [[bounty hunter]]s and the finest agents of [[Lord Helmawr]]. The Imperial House is justifiably fearful of the potential consequences this creature's presence could have on the future of Necromunda.{{Fn|4}}

Hernot.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
'''Hernot''' was a [[Junior Officer]] in the [[Astra Militarum]].{{Fn|4}}
==History==
He was among{{Fn|4}} [[Astra Militarum|its forces]] that the [[Inquisitor Lord]] [[Severus Oln]]{{Fn|3}} hastily gathered, to confront{{Fn|1}} the [[Chaos Warband|Warband]] of the [[Nurgle]] [[Sorcerer]] [[Septic Lexus]].{{Fn|2}} Oln's pursuit of the Warband led his forces to [[Tikgrix]], where the Inquisitor Lord originally thought he would be dealing with a routine [[Chaos Cult]] purging. However he soon began sensing{{Fn|1}} a [[Great Unclean One]]{{Fn|5}} within his mind, which was trapped within a cube prison in a village on Tikgrix. Lexus intended to break the prison open, and Oln realized at once, that he was not prepared to face{{Fn|1}} the [[Greater Daemon]].{{Fn|6}} Instead the Inquisitor Lord resolved to stop the Sorcerer from freeing the Great Unclean One and then a cell of Inquisitors or [[Grey Knight]]s would later deal with the Greater Daemon.{{Fn|1}} 

The two sides then clashed in the village,{{Fn|5}} all while the [[Greater Daemon]] attacked their minds to dominate them.{{Fn|6}} Unfortunately, Hernot{{Fn|4}} and many of [[Severus Oln|Oln]]'s forces fell under its sway and this greatly aided{{Fn|6}} [[Septic Lexus|Lexus]] in successfully freeing the [[Great Unclean One]]. The [[Inquisitor Lord]] was then killed in battle with the [[Sorcerer]] and the newly freed [[Daemon]], who soon unleashed the forces of the [[Chaos God]] [[Nurgle]] upon the world. This led to the deaths of Hernot and Oln's remaining retinue and the Great Unclean One{{Fn|5}} began to change Tikgrix into a [[Daemon World]].{{Fn|1}} 
==Trivia==
''Hernot'' and [[Severus Oln]] were created by the [[Games Workshop]] employee [[Bryan Barnes]] and they were featured on an older version of the company's website.{{Fn|3}}

Heth.wikitext:
{{ImperialGuardPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was [[Lord Commander Militant]] of the [[Imperial Guard]] during mid-[[M32]]. A primary rival on the [[Senatorum Imperialis]] to [[Lord High Admiral]] [[Lansung]], Heth was different from the Admiral due to his desire to lead from the front lines and close relationship with the common rank and file. Heth was part of the anti-Lansung faction on the High Lords that included [[Inquisitorial Representative]] [[Wienand]] and [[Grand Master of Assassins]] [[Drakan Vangorich]].{{Fn|1a}}

During the [[War of the Beast]], Heth personally led an expeditionary force to relieve the [[Imperial Fists]] on [[Ardamantua]] from a massive [[Ork]] force. However Heth's forces were quickly annihilated, and before his ship was seemingly destroyed the Lord Commander Militant dispatched a message back to [[Terra]] warning of [[The Beast]] and his [[Attack Moon]].{{Fn|1b}}

Hexas.wikitext:
{{ImperialFistsPortal}}
'''Hexas''' was an [[Imperial Fist]], who took part in the [[Horus Heresy]]'s [[Siege of Terra]].{{Fn|1}} 
==History==
He was later among the [[Imperial Fists]]{{Fn|1}} that the [[Loyalist Legion|Legion]]'s [[Primarch]], [[Rogal Dorn]], commanded as part of the [[Emperor]]'s [[Teleportation]] boarding attack upon the [[Sons of Horus]]' flagship, the [[Vengeful Spirit]].{{Fn|2a}} They were tasked with killing the [[Traitor|traitorous]] Primarch [[Horus]], in order to save [[Terra]] and the [[Imperium]], but due to Horus' machinations, the Emperor's boarding party was separated from each other.{{Fn|2b}} Worse still for the Imperial Fists aboard the Vengeful Spirit, Dorn had also been torn away from them{{Fn|2c}} and so the [[Huscarls (Imperial Fists)|Huscarl]] [[Diamantis]] took command of the Legion's forces. However the Imperial Forces would all be killed, after they were swarmed by Horus' forces and their remains were later found by a grief stricken Rogal Dorn, who swore to avenge their deaths.{{Fn|1}}

Heyd Calder.wikitext:
{{ImperialFistsPortal}}
[[File:ApocalypseClear.jpeg|200px|thumb|Heyd Calder (center){{Fn|2}}]]
'''Heyd Calder''' is a [[Space Marine Lieutenant|Lieutenant]] of the [[Imperial Fists]] 3rd Company{{Fn|1a}}. 

==History==
A [[Huscarl]], Calder was assigned to lead a force of Imperial Fists, [[Raven Guard]], and [[White Scars]] to the [[Cardinal World]] of [[Almace]] at the behest of [[Cardinal]]-[[Governor]] [[Eamon]], who was [[Invasion of the Odoacer System|under attack]] by the [[Word Bearers]] [[Chaos Lord]] [[Amatnim Ur-Nabas Lash]].{{Fn|1a}} Upon arriving at Almace alongside [[Suboden Khan]] and Lieutenant [[Sael Karros]], he navigated the political intrigue of the [[Ecclesiarchy]] court as he attempted to fortify Almace against the incoming Word Bearers invasion.{{Fn|1b}}

Calder is shocked to discover that Eamon was harboring a seemingly loyalist Word Bearer [[Dreadnought]] beneath Almace for millennia, dubbed [[The Anchorite]], and that the Word Bearers were there to retrieve him.{{Fn|1c}} In the final battle against the Word Bearers, Calder led a desperate attempt on the Ecclesiarchy palace walls, holding the Cardinal Gate as The Anchorite was freed by Eamon.{{Fn|1d}} As the Word Bearers breach the walls, Calder confronted Amatnim and engaged him in a duel. Amatnim is able to hold off Calder, but is beset upon by The Anchorite. Amatnim experiences a spiritual crisis after witnessing Anchorite's divine powers and willingly allows Calder to kill him.{{Fn|1e}}

Calder oversaw a loyalist victory on [[Almace]], but at heavy cost.{{Fn|1e}}

Hieronyma.wikitext:
{{AdeptusMechanicusPortal}}
'''Hieronyma''' was a [[Magos Dominus|Magos Domina]] of the [[Ordo Reductor]] during the [[Horus Heresy]]. She ascended to become '''the Archimandrite''' at the behest of [[Fabricator General]] [[Zagreus Kane|Kane]] and took command of the [[Mechanicum]]'s military forces in the [[War Within the Webway]].{{Fn|1a}}

==The Archimandrite==
'''The Archimandrite''' was an avatar of the [[Omnissiah|Unmaker God]], a fusion of '''Hieronyma''''s brain with a weaponised chassis similar to that of a [[Domitar Class Robot]]{{Fn|1b}} created with forbidden lore from the [[Hexarchion Vaults]]. It included clawed feet, fists capable of crushing [[power armour]] with [[flamer|flamers]] in the wrists and shoulder-mounted [[Volkite Weapon|Volkite]] and [[Avenger Bolt Cannon|Avenger Bolt]] cannons. One hand also mounted a double-barrelled energy weapon that produced fusion beams, a rare gift from [[Arkhan Land]].{{fn|1c}}

When the daemonic hordes overwhelmed [[Calastar]], the Archimandrite ordered all Mechanicum forces to abandon the retreating Imperial forces in a bid to locate and defend the [[Aresian Path]]. Most of them were killed or lost before they could converge on its position. The person of Hieronyma resurfaced moments before she was forcibly [[Daemonic Possession|possessed]] by the daemon [[Drach'nyen]].{{fn|1d}} The body of the Archimandrite was destroyed by [[Knight#Society|Baroness]] [[Jaya D'Arcus]] of [[House Vyridion]].{{fn|1e}}

[[Image:Hieronymus Doloroso.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Portrait of Hieronymus Doloroso{{Fn|2}}]]
'''Hieronymus Doloroso''' was a [[Ministorum]] [[Priest]] and [[Missionary]] as of [[M42]]. He was a diehard believer of the [[Drusians|Drusian Faith]], leading the [[Imperial Cult]] in the [[Koronus Sector]] from [[Footfall]]. He has many negative things to say about the rest of the Ecclesiarchy whom he thinks are vain and prideful. He considers himself the personal [[Confessor]] and guide of [[Rogue Trader]] [[Incedia Chorda]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
In the past, he was an [[Administratum]] [[Adept]] who successfully led his homeworld to economic prosperity. He was too successful, and the planet soon turned to decadence and vice, causing a complete moral collapse and the loss of millions of lives. He sees his fanaticism for the Drusian Faith and his current work as penance for this past failure which he feels he will never be able to redeem himself for.{{Fn|1}}

Hiram Sult.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Hiram Sult''' was a [[Rogue Trader]] and was a scion of [[House Sult]]. He was active in the [[Koronus Expanse]] in the 700's.[[M41]].{{Fn|1b}}

==History==
His House entered into a blood feud with [[House Marner]] in 520.[[M41]] when they clashed in the [[Battle of Embers]].{{Fn|1a}}

In 747.[[M41]], Hiram unexpectedly rediscovered the lost [[colony world]] [[Sunerisle]], on the edge of the [[Accursed Demesne]]. However, he soon learned that its settlements were rife with the taint of the [[Genestealer]] and Hiram barely escaped from the world with his life; many of Hiram's crew that accompanied him were not so lucky. When he returned to his fleet, Hiram had Sunerisle [[Orbital Bombardment|bombarded from orbit]] with every plasma warhead in his arsenal, just to be sure the Genestealers were destroyed.{{Fn|1b}}

Hlaine Larkin.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
[[Image:Hlaine Larkin.jpg|thumb|right|330px|'''Hlaine Larkin''', Tanith 1st.{{Fn|15}}]]
[[Trooper]] '''Hlaine Larkin''', also known as '''Mad Larkin''', '''Mad Larks''' or simply '''Larks''', was an [[Imperial Guard Sniper]] in the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment]].{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|3a}} He served in this role almost from the inception of the regiment, swiftly becoming recognised as the regiment's pre-eminent marksman. As a result of his elite status, Larkin was regularly selected for special operations assignments and amassed a noteworthy service record as a result.


==Biography==
{{Spoiler|source=Gaunt's Ghosts (Novel Series)}}
===Early Career===
Originally a hunter in Tanith's nalwood forests, Hlaine Larkin later served alongside [[Forgal]] and [[Colm Corbec]] in the [[Tanith Magna]] militia before joining the Guard as part of the originally founded Tanith regiments, sharing a tent with [[Colm Corbec]] and [[Elim Rawne]] on the night before the regiment was to ship out.{{Fn|2a}} He survived the razing of [[Tanith]] and his sniper abilities quickly elevated him to an elite status within the regiment.

Larkin was in his early fifties when he enlisted.{{Fn|3a}} Though he was the Tanith's premier sniper, Larkin was also mentally unstable, suffering from anxiety-related migraines, fits, and delusions.{{Fn|2b}} One of Larkin's eccentricities was that he believed the scope of his long-las would always show him the truth, no matter what delusions he was suffering.{{Fn|2b}}{{Fn|3a}} The apparent truth of this superstition was proved on [[Monthax]], when looking through the scope allowed Larkin to see through the illusions cast by [[Eldar]] [[Farseer]] [[Eon Kull]].{{Fn|2c}}

On [[Bucephalon]] Larkin succumbed to terror and abandoned his comrades, winding up in an abandoned church where he hallucinated that a statue of [[Saint Sabbat]] was talking to him. With the help of this 'angel' Larkin was able to kill the enemy [[Magister]] [[Nokad the Blighted]], a significant early victory for the Ghosts.{{Fn|2b}}

During the campaign on [[Fortis Binary]] Larkin was attached to the regiment's first squad as its sniper.{{Fn|1a}} In this role, he ended up attached to [[Colonel]] [[Colm Corbec|Corbec's]] [[Imperial Guard Company|company]] during the Tanith counter-attack that would act as the catalyst for Imperial victory (the regiment was heavily dispersed by shellfire at the onset of the attack, and it is unknown if Larkin's squad actually belonged to Corbec's company) and was soon after attached to an ad hoc scout team the Colonel created, led by [[Imperial Guard Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Grell]].{{Fn|1b}} This scout team led the rest of the company into linking up with the bulk of the dispersed regiment, behind enemy lines. After achieving unit cohesion, the Tanith 1st, with the aid of the [[Vitrian Dragoons]], penetrated the [[Shriven (Chaos Cult)|Shriven]] defences, in an attack in which Larkin used the [[Needler|Needle-pattern]] [[sniper rifle]] he was then issued with to seriously wound an [[Iron Warriors]] [[Chaos Space Marine]], as well as slay a host of more [[human]] enemies.{{Fn|1c}}

In the rest and recuperation period afterwards, Larkin took time out to visit illegal gambling dens on the world of [[Pyrites]] in the company of [[Trooper]] [[Bragg]], as well as get tangled up in an incident with the [[Jantine Patricians regiment]] that would lead to a blood-feud.{{Fn|1d}}

This feud developed murderously while both regiments were in-transit to their next combat theatre in the [[Menazoid Clasp]], both because of the feud's natural ire and because it was the will of the Jantines' secret patron, [[Inquisitor]] [[Heldane]]. Larkin became directly involved when [[Major]] [[Rawne]] of the Tanith was kidnapped by the Jantine and delivered over to Heldane for torture. Larkin was assigned to the revenge squad sent to cause havoc and get Rawne back{{Fn|1e}}; during this successful rescue he shot Heldane (not knowing he was an Inquisitor at the time) in the throat with a bullet from the solid-round, bolt-action rifle he had recently gained as a spoil of war, critically wounding the [[radical]] Inquisitor.{{Fn|1f}}

Larkin then deployed onto [[Menazoid Epsilon]] with the rest of the regiment, being seconded once again to a special squad, this time the commando unit formed from hand-picked members of the Tanith and [[Navy Intelligence]], which penetrated a secret underground complex upon the world and discovered a working [[Standard Template Constructor]].{{Fn|1g}}{{Fn|1h}} Ultimately, the [[STC]] was proven to be corrupted when it produced several tainted and hostile [[Men of Iron]], which the survivors of the commando team - including Larkin - briefly engaged with in close quarters combat before retreating and blowing up the entire facility.{{Fn|1i}}{{Fn|1j}}

In the closing stages of the [[Siege of Vervunhive]], Larkin was one of thirty Tanith selected personally by [[Colonel-Commissar]] [[Ibram Gaunt]] to take part in [[Operation Heironymo]], the mission to infiltrate [[The Spike]] and assassinate [[Heritor Asphodel]].{{Fn|3b}}

===New Blood===
Of all the talented marksmen in the Ghosts, Larkin was the only one to maintain his reputation against the scratch-company markswomen who joined the regiment following the [[Siege of Vervunhive]] such as [[Nessa Bourah]], [[Jessi Banda]] and [[Sehra Muril]]. However, he soon developed a deeply negative relationship with another new Verghastite trooper, [[Lijah Cuu]], whose psychotic behavior disturbed Larkin{{Fn|4}}{{Fn|5a}} even before Cuu murdered Larkin's best friend [[Bragg]] in the aftermath of [[Operation Larisel]]{{Fn|5b}}, in which Larkin took part.{{Fn|5a}}

By the time the Tanith joined the campaign on [[Aexe Cardinal]] Larkin and Cuu had become mortal enemies, with Cuu making two attempts on Larkin's life - once in an abandoned section of trench before being interrupted by enemy shelling, and a brutal second attack in an abandoned manor house in the Montorq Forest, where Cuu beat Larkin over the head with a skillet before being kicked in the testicles by Sehra Muril.{{Fn|6a}}{{Fn|6b}} Larkin later confided in Muril his suspicion that Cuu had murdered Bragg and Muril convinced him that murdering Cuu in revenge was not the solution, but this turned out to be a mistake, as Cuu later murdered Muril under the cover of a [[Blood Pact]] assault on the manor.{{Fn|6c}} Larkin eventually got his revenge on [[Herodor]] when Cuu was possessed by enemy psykers and used as a puppet to try and killed the Beati, but while Larkin killed Cuu with a headshot he was too late to stop the traitor from mowing down Colonel [[Corbec]], another of Larkin's oldest friends.{{Fn|7a}}

After the events on Herodor, Larkin was chosen for the EZ-level mission to [[Gereon]]. Colonel-Commissar Gaunt was concerned about how Larkin would cope with the intense mental pressure of operating on an enemy-held planet, but Larkin's sniper skills made him too valuable not to include, and surprisingly coping with the situation on Gereon seemed to strengthen Larkin's mental health, to the point that he no longer suffered anxiety, migraines or delusions after returning to the regiment. However, Larkin's physical health was impacted upon the regiment's return to Gereon, when a Chaos tank drove over and crushed his left foot. Gaunt amputated the foot with his power sword, and Larkin was later fitted with a simple replacement which gave him a limp but did not affect his marksmanship.{{Fn|8}}{{Fn|9a}}

Like the rest of the Ghosts, Larkin was haunted by visions of lost comrades during the final stages of the assault on [[Hinzerhaus]] during the [[Jago]] campaign, but visions of Bragg and Corbec proved encouraging and even Cuu's menacing presence only served to sharpen Larkin's focus and determination.{{Fn|10a}} Larkin would survive the desperate defence and went on to enjoy a year's regimental sabbatical on [[Balhaut]], where he saved Gaunt by assassinating the leader of a Blood Pact strike team sent to kill an enemy defector Gaunt was protecting.{{Fn|10a}} Later, during the mission to [[Salvation's Reach]], Larkin took it upon himself to help his old comrade [[Rhen Merrt]] recover his lost marksmanship skill, and acted as sniper for one of the minesweeping teams which infiltrated the enemy research station.{{Fn|12a}}{{Fn|12b}} He then fought in the battle for [[Urdesh]], which ended with the death of [[Anakwanar Sek]] and a massive Imperial victory.{{Fn|13}}

==Appearance and Abilities==
Larkin was a wiry, pale and generally unhealthy-looking man during his time in the Guard, which he joined in his late forties or early fifties. He wore three silver hoop earrings in his left ear and had a blue spiral wyrm tattoo on his right cheek.{{Fn|1a}}

After the fracas on the ship en route to [[Menazoid Epsilon]], he retained the bolt-action rifle he had taken from the Jantines' trophy hall as a "lucky charm," since he had used it to fell Inquisitor Heldane.{{Fn|1h}}

He is described by his friend [[Colm Corbec|Colm]] as having a marksman's eye and a brave heart but tempered with an unstable character.

'''Hol Beloth''' was a senior [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]]{{fn|2}} of the [[Word Bearers]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] during the [[Horus Heresy]].

===History===
Beloth gained infamy during the [[Great Crusade]] for purging billions of [[human]]s on [[Serenity Alpha]] after condemning their decadent lifestyle that relied completely on robotics and technology.{{Fn|3}}

An extremely ambitious individual, Beloth was eager to become more a commander than a conduit, to achieve a higher purpose standing at the side of [[Lorgar|Lorgar Aurelian]] as [[Erebus]] and [[Kor Phaeron]] did. [[First Chaplain]] Erebus and Beloth's own [[Dark Apostle]] [[Maloq Kartho]] encouraged his ambitions.{{Fn|1a}}

During the [[Battle of Calth]], Beloth was one of the [[Space Marine Commander|Force Commander]]s selected for the assault, charged with taking and securing [[Lanshear]] for the Word Bearers.{{Fn|1a}} When [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Remus Ventanus]] lead the [[Ultramarines]] 4th Company into Lanshear to secure a [[cogitator]] with a kill-code, Beloth soon realized that they were attempting to achieve something specific and unleashed [[Titan]]s, [[Terminator]]s, and the [[Gal Vorbak]] upon the Ultramarines.{{Fn|1b}} Before his forces could finish off the 4th, reinforcements from the Ultramarines 19th, 111th and 112th Companies under Captain [[Aethon]] and [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Anchise]], Titans and Land Raiders under [[Tetrarch of Ultramar|Tetrarch]] [[Tauro Nicodemus]], and the Neride 41st under Tetrarch [[Eikos Lamiad]] and the [[Contemptor Pattern Dreadnought]] [[Telemechrus]] arrived to reinforce Ventanus. The strength and coordination of the reinforcements shocked Beloth's forces and two of his senior captains were killed by Telemechrus. While this effectively served to concentrate Hol Beloth's victims into one place, the tide soon turned on the Word Bearers when [[Magos]] [[Meer Edv Tawren]] took control of the planetary defense grid and opened fire on the Word Bearers from orbit, obliterating most of Beloth's forces.{{fn|1c}}

His ambitions shattered, Beloth retreated with the rest of his surviving forces into the Uranik Radial arcology as Calth's sun turned radioactive. Safely underground he brooded on his failure until Maloq Kartho goaded him into joining the [[Underworld War]], taking the fight to the Ultramarines once more. Beloth joined a strike team led by Kartho which recovered a [[virus bomb]] from the surface and followed Kartho up a damaged skyscraper from which the two of them could see Remus Ventanus's forces attacking the stronghold of [[Foedral Fell]]. Kartho then detonated an atomic bomb which wiped out the Uranik Radial, sacrificing Beloth's forces to further his bid for [[Daemonhood|daemonhood]] and collapsing the skyscraper into a deep cave system. Remarkably Beloth survived the fall and was able to join Kartho's assault on Arcology X, stronghold of Ventanus's forces which had been left lightly defended whilst Ventanus took his forces to assault Foedral Fell. During the battle Beloth mutated into an unstoppable [[daemon]], and was only slain when Ventanus detonated a pair of grenades within his body and revealed Beloth's subsumed [[athame]], which Ventanus used to slay the mutated former commander.{{Fn|4}}

Honorius (Warmaster).wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
'''Honorius''' was an [[Imperial]] [[Lord Militant]] and later on the [[Warmaster]] of the [[Ophidian Campaign]].{{Fn|1a}}

Before embarking on the Ophidian Campaign, Lord Militant Honorius was responsible for pacifying the [[Helican Schism]], a mass uprising in the [[Helican Subsector]].{{Fn|1a}} The pacification efforts took eight months{{Fn|2}} and, to Honorius' great displeasure, heavily delayed the start of the Ophidian Campaign.{{Fn|1a}} 

After the conclusion of the successful Ophidian Campaign, Honorius was to be given the title of ''Feudal Protector'' by the [[Sector Lord|Imperial Lord Commander Helican]] [[Jeromya Faurlitz IV]] for his achievements during the campaign. Honorius' success made him a prime candidate to succeed the late Warmaster [[Hiju]] on the [[Acrotara]] theatre. Warmaster Hiju had been groomed for a spot in the [[Senatorum Imperialis]] and perhaps even to sit amongst the [[High Lords of Terra]]. In succeeding Hiju, Honorius could have become a notable candidate for the spot as well.{{Fn|1b}}

On [[Thracian Primaris]] during the victory parade of the Ophidian Campaign{{Fn|1e}} and the bestowment of Honorius' new title as the ''Feudal Protector''{{Fn|1a}}, the parade was attacked by the forces of [[Chaos]].{{Fn|1e}} Honorius' forces had captured thirty-three [[heretic]] [[psykers]] of level [[The Assignment|alpha]] or above at [[Dolsene]] during the final engagement of the Ophidian Campaign.{{Fn|1c}} These imprisoned psykers were on display at the parade. Honorius took great delight in displaying his dangerous, now seemingly harmaless enemies to the cheering populace. Despite the heavy security measures around the psykers{{Fn|1d}}, the attack managed to set them free and let them cause havok on a catastrophic scale.{{Fn|1e}} This event would later on be known as the [[Thracian_Primaris#The_Triumph|Thracian Atrocity]].{{Fn|1h}} Warmaster Honorius was heavily injured in the attack and required immediate emergency surgery. He was transported to a medical frigate at the [[Imperial Navy|navy]]-yard where he received medical treatment.{{Fn|1f}} On the sixth day of the resulting unrest, it was announced that the Warmaster would live.{{Fn|1g}}

In the vision, the [[Emperor]] told Hormoth to dig within an area located between [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]]'s [[Dust Sea]] and the ruins of [[Hive Bellium]]. The [[Thane (House Cawdor)|Thane]] did as he was told and after an eventful journey, and the loss of hundreds of his followers, Hormoth reached the location described in the vision. He then began digging and unearthed a strangely glowing bone fragment, which was said to be from [[Imperial Saint|Saint]] [[Valdorus]]. Hormoth then proudly wore the bone around his neck, until he mysteriously died soon afterwards.

{{otheruses|USE=inquisitor involved in the [[Second War for Armageddon]]|OTHERUSE=inquisitor involved in the [[Gothic War]]|OTHERPAGE=Thadus Valconet Horst}}
[[Inquisitor]] '''Horst''' was born on a planet ruled by an evil Overlord named [[Alaine de Briant]].  At an early age he joined a freedom fighter group, quickly rising through the ranks to become their leader as his extraordinary fighting ability showed itself in many battles.

He was not just a good fighter, but had excellent oratory skills as well as great charm, and using these traits he united the rebel factions that were fighting against the Overlord.  He fought a brilliant guerrilla campaign against the overlord and eventually, against all the odds, he overthrew the Overlord after almost thirty years of bitter warfare.

When news of his work reached the [[Administratum]], he was quickly inducted into the [[Inquisition]], at a relatively late age.

Several years later, he happened to be on a [[Squat]] planet near [[Armageddon]].  When the [[Second War for Armageddon]] began, he was quickly able to convince the Squat Overlord to send troops to help.  As soon as the [[Warp Storm]] lifted, Horst and a large army of Squats landed on [[Armageddon Prime]] where they quickly pushed the [[Ork]]s back onto the defensive.  After the defeat of the Orks at [[Tartarus Hive]], Horst led a massive assault, forcing the Orks back to the jungle area between the two areas, [[Armageddon Prime]] and [[Armageddon Secundus]].
